utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please stand and read the affirmation on the card that is now given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I don't believe we have officially called the witness. We would call Witness M-017 at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, to assist the Chamber because there are a number of documents that the Prosecution intends to exhibit through this witness, we have prepared similar binders, what we'll call witness binders, containing these proposed exhibits in hard copy for the Chambers. The exhibits, however, will be displayed through e-court. If we could distribute those now. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could I please have the usher's assistance in providing the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could I please have the usher's assistance in providing the witness with a document that bears ERN number 0424-7790? I'm sorry, Mr. Usher. I don't believe it's in the witness binder. I have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at this piece of paper that is before you and tell us whether, without reading any of the names or any of the information out loud, whether the names written on this -- whether there are two names written on this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you please tell us if the second name that appears on this piece of paper is the correct spelling of your legal name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is the first name that appears on this piece of paper the correct spelling of your legal name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: The name is correctly spelled and the last name as well, even though the letters must be small, but it's okay. It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we may go into private session briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And if the identification sheet could now be shown to the Defence, please. Do you, in due course, tender that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The identification sheet will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P13, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, we've now moved into public session, so that you know. Directing your attention to the date --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Directing your attention to the date August -- 12 August 2001, were you in the basement of a residence in the village where you were during that time-period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I can tell you what I know right from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, my question to you was: Were you in the basement of a residence in the village where you were? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. I was in a basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Without mentioning any names of any other people, can you tell us why you were there in that basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: We were there -- the entire family was there. It was a basement where we felt secure from the uninterrupted shelling of the police, the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You say "uninterrupted shelling of the police, the army." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. If you allow me, I'd like to express what I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if you could just answer my question. When I asked you about uninterrupted shelling, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. It was continuous shelling by the army, and we were obliged to enter into a basement where we felt safer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm showing you what -- 65 ter 178, page 40. It is tab 2 of today's binder bearing ERN N003-0346. Witness, do you see the photo before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, and I recognise it. I know what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if you could just tell me, if you could take the stylus -- well, first of all, could you tell us what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I'm looking at the location where we were lying face down. This is the entrance to the house of -- and I'm not going to mention the name if we are in public session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you -- could you mark for us, please, using the stylus the area where you were -- you say you were lying down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And just for the record, the witness has marked with a blue line, actually, a lose rectangular form in the bottom left, partly centre portion of the photograph. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you have told us that at some point, you were at this location. Did you see anything happen to your brother at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: After we were forced to take the direction of Ljubanci village, there was shooting. We thought that they were going to kill us. We were quite frightened, but in such situations you cannot actually define how frightened you are, when you know that you are in the hands of savage people.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, could I interrupt you for a second, please? If you could just listen to my question and just answer it as briefly as you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, to be safe, perhaps we should move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You tender the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P17, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you've indicated that you were --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you indicated that you were ordered to walk to Ljubanci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did you arrive at some location after this walk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to tell you now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If you can just wait for my question, Witness. When you -- what location did you arrive at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: After we were forced to leave in the direction of Ljubanci, we arrived at the exit of Ljuboten and the entrance point to Ljubanci. And there is a house called Brace's house. It belongs to this person Braca.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask again for the usher's assistance in showing you another photograph, which is tab 5 of the binder prepared for today. It's 65 ter number 199, page 132, bearing ERN N004-4571. Is also photograph B from page 13 of the Court binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you tendering --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I just caught that. Thank you, Your Honour. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 201, page 60, will become Exhibit P19, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could that last exhibit be tendered under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph that's before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, even though it doesn't seem to be right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I think we can adjust that. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. It is the place we were at when we were lying down on our stomachs on this place. I can encircle the place where we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could, with the assistance of the usher, take the stylus and mark on the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has marked with a blue circle towards the bottom right corner in the road depicted in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you walked to this location from the house where you were. What happened at this location to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: When we arrived there, there was a hermeline which first entered the village, and it had stopped there. And when we arrived there, they ordered us to lie down on our stomachs, and a woman, I can mention her name -- not her name, but her husband's name, she said, You haven't done short work of terrorists yet? And very savagely they started to beat us. I don't know how to describe it. All the policemen who were there started to get on our backs to kick us and to hit us, to jump on us as if we were animals. I wouldn't have done what they did to us to an animal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did you see anyone at this location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: The then minister, this person who is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could show a video clip -- I'm sorry. Could we please tender the last photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P20, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we show the video clip on sanction, which is 65 ter number 309, ERN V000-3494. The clip is at 6 minutes, 24 seconds to 6 minutes 31 seconds. It is referenced on tab 12 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at the screen at the video clip that is about to be displayed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, did you see the video clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and I saw also the then minister. If you want me, I can circle his face.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: No, that's fine. Did you know the then minister's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Walpita, could you put the ending of the clip back up?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we do not see the picture on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Nor do we.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you still see the same video clip that was displayed earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I know you told me that you recognise the person, the then minister. Could you tell me, please, in reference to the clip that you're seeing, which person that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: May I mark the face, or you want me to indicate with my finger?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you please describe what the person is wearing; maybe that's easiest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. He is wearing not an army or police uniform, but a normal suit without any uniform. He is in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what colour the person is wearing, what colour clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Black. Black clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is there anyone else in this video clip that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. The minister knows that he was a police agent, in Bit Pazar My brother at the time used to sell backhoe in Bit Pazar. My brothers know him, each though I personally never sold, I was -- tobacco or something. I was only 13 at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: This person that you're referring to, was he a police agent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in reference to the video clip, could you tell us what this person in the video clip is wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: He's wearing a white T-shirt and you can see the colour very well, because it's there. It's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 21, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you described for -- you described beatings that occurred at this location that you marked earlier. Could you tell us were you transferred -- transported anywhere after this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you leave that area, Ms. Motoike, it is not clear from what has been said whether the witness is saying that he saw the accused Mr. Boskoski there that day at that scene, or whether he is simply saying that he has seen the film clip later and identifies Mr. Boskoski in that film clip. I think it could be important to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you -- you indicated that in the video clip that that's Mr. Boskoski. Did you see Mr. Boskoski that day, on the 12th August 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. It is written also in the statement, but I will show you. We were with T-shirts on our heads, and I would say quite stealthily I managed to look from the tail of my eye because they didn't allow to us see, and I saw only the face of the then minister who is being charged. Even though, as I said, I had the T-shirt on my head, it prevented me from seeing clearly what clothes he was wearing. But to me, it seemed they were of a black colour. Whether it was really black or not, I cannot ascertain, but this is how they seemed to me. But his face, I could see very well and I could recognise. So I may certify that I saw his face, but I cannot say that he was wearing police or army uniform, but plain civilian clothes in black colour, at least this is how it looked to me. So I can always -- I can again say that I saw him, actually saw him that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, where did you see Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Here, where we were, sitting in front of the Brace's house. And he appeared in front of us in front of that tank or whatever that vehicle was. And he was telling the police, Well done, you have caught the terrorists. Even though he knew pretty well who we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you referred to the photograph in your -- in your answer just now, you referred to the photograph that's still remaining on your desk. And you said "It's this place." The photograph that's on your desk presently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Does that photograph -- I'm sorry, can I inquire what the photograph is that's still remaining on the desk? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: This is at Brace's House.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It's tab 5 of today's binder. 65 ter 199, page 132. If we could perhaps display this on e-court as well. And for the record, I believe it has already been marked as P20. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, is this the photograph -- do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is this the photograph that you were referring to when you said that "This is where I saw Mr. Boskoski"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And some point, Witness, after -- after you were beaten at this location, were you transported somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Here I lost consciousness. I fainted, because of the beating, of the severe beating that was inflicted on us. And after that, I wasn't aware of where I was. But when I regained consciousness, it was at the police station in Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And by "here," are you referring to the location still that is indicated in P20, the photograph, that's before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please? I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You stated that you lost consciousness and you referred to a location. Is the location depicted in photograph P20, that is before you right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, from this place where I -- which I see on the photo. After that, I wasn't aware. Yes, the place you see on this photo. And when I regained consciousness it was at the police station in Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps a break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will need to adjourn now for the tapes to be changed and we'll resume at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, before our recess, you indicated that you were taken to a location called Mirkovci police station. How were you treated at Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: As if we were beasts. I regained consciousness, as I indicated earlier, but there were times that I fainted, too, but there are witnesses who will testify about how we were treated in Mirkovci police station. Before they received us at Mirkovci police station, because the commander of the police station refused to accept us there as we were, I would say, 99 per cent dead, in such terrible condition, they put us in a kind of a basement, not exactly a basement but it was a covered area, and they threw water on us, using a hose, just to make all of us regain consciousness. And after that, they put us inside the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, can I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we go into private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, were you ever hospitalised during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I would like to add something with regard to the Mirkovci police station. When we were taken inside the police station, I don't know for how long I was unconscious, but I would like to tell you that in this police station I regained consciousness. Not that I was feeling well, but I felt that I was still alive. I asked one of the policemen in the room who were standing at the door there, I asked him to allow me to go and drink some water. He immediately reacted harshly and he hit me once again. They continued to beat us. I again asked for permission to go to the toilet. They responded in the same manner. As I said earlier, we were almost dead, 99 per cent dead, and a human being, a real human being cannot do this to another human being. It is very difficult for me to explain this. Maybe we should go to a closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, could I stop you there, please. You described that they continued to beat us. What did they beat you with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: You know what the police carries. They beat us with rifle-butts, with baseball bats, batons. They used everything to hit us. A human being cannot do this kind of things to another human being.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. My question to you earlier was: Were you ever hospitalised during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. I will tell you now about the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if you could just wait for my question. Can I ask you how you were treated at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: They came and we said to them that we want to go to the hospital. Usually people go to a hospital to get a treatment. Among those who went, it was me --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, before you mention any names, my question to you was: How did the people -- how were you treated at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: When we arrived at the hospital, we thought that we were going to get a proper treatment. However, even at the hospital they beat us. Even the doctors were hitting us. I asked the doctor to bring me some water, and he -- I asked him in a humanly manner, Can I get some water? And he replied, he said, I would not give you poison let alone water. This is what I want through while in the hospital. They were hitting the others as well. There were policemen inside the hospital as well. I saw how they were hitting him, and because of the power of the blow, that person jumped so high up to the ceiling. It is so difficult for me to -- to explain in words what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, could I stop you there, please. You said that the doctors were hitting you and that policemen as well. What did these people hit you with, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: The policemen were armed at all times. They were hitting us with rifle-butts while the doctor would hit us with his fists or kick us, in all possible ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, do you know what hospital this was that you were transported to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: The city hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And when you arrived at the hospital, were you told what kind of injuries you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: As I already said, we went there to get a treatment, but they didn't ask us at all about our injuries. As I already said, we were almost 99 per cent dead. Except for an infusion, nothing else they tried to bring us back to life with these infusions, but -- with IVs just to be able to continue and hit us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance in showing to the witness 65 ter 220, and, Your Honours, I would ask permission for these documents that I'm going to show the witness for them not to be published to the public. It is tab 15 of today's Court binder or witness binder bearing ERN N000-5177, the Macedonian version; and the English version is N000-5174, N000-5180, ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You asked there be an order for no public publication. The basis for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the documents actually I'm now going into a few with the witness and the documents that I refer to have not only the name of this particular witness, but I believe other witnesses who are also under protective measures in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, there should be no publication beyond this courtroom of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you see before you a document, and if I could draw your attention to the upper left corner of the Macedonian version? Do you see your name indicated in that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I don't see my name mentioned on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Looking at the version that is in front of you now, do you see in the -- well, first of all, let me ask you, do you read the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the name that's in the upper left corner of the Macedonian version of this document that's being displayed in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Does this document indicate a date? If I didn't ask you, is that your name that appears in that corner of the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, it's my name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the bottom of this document in the left-hand corner, do you see a date there of 14 November 2003?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you also see that this -- in the bottom right-hand corner of this document, there is also a seal with a doctor's name indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention to the first paragraph, perhaps with the usher's assistance, the first full paragraph of that document. I believe there's a date reference there, 13/8/2001. Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It says on 13th August 2001 --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Without going into details, can you tell me is your name mentioned in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to read this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No. I don't think I had this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you take a moment just to read the first two sentences of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I read this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And for the record, the first paragraph indicates that on 13 August 2001, Witness M-017 was brought to the clinic by ambulance with head injuries. At admission, the patient was conscious, responsive, said he had briefly fallen unconsciousness after receiving the injury. Those are the first two sentences that I asked the witness to read.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell me, does this paragraph describe -- accurately describes the injuries that you had when you were taken to the hospital on the date you described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: The document mentions that I was unconscious but does not mention at all my injuries and the nature of my injuries. We were all injured. This document says that they X-rayed me and examined me, which is a big lie. What this document says is not true. There is some truth as for my unconsciousness, but as for other claims that they have allegedly X-rayed or examined me, that is not true. They only contributed to the deterioration of my health condition.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If this document could be tendered, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P22, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, at some point were you released from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. I was released from the hospital and taken straight to prison. Actually, it was necessary for me to spend at least one month, not to say three months because of my injuries; however, they took me from the hospital straight to the Sutka prison, although I did not deserve to go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, my mistake, I would like that last exhibit, P22, to be admitted under seal. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can it be clear that it's only the one page that you are seeking to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The single page that we showed the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At Sutka prison, Witness, how were you treated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, personally, I cannot claim here things that I did not experience. Only one policeman or people working in the prison hit me just once and ordered me to go to my room. I could hardly stand on my feet there. Actually, I had to walk on my fours to get there. I could hardly stand on my feet. There were people there who were beaten as well, but they will testify for themselves. As for me personally, this person only hit me once. The others will tell you about their own experience in the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you said that you were in Sutka prison for how long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: How long? Four months. I spent four months in Sutka prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At some point then, you were released. Do you know why you were released from prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Why I was released from prison?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Well, when I was released from prison, the former president of the state, Boris Trajkovski issued a document that amnestied us. Calling us terrorists and amnestied as terrorists, although we were not terrorists. This is what the others called us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to show you another document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could display 65 ter 155. It is tab 13 of today's binder bearing ERN N000-9720, N000-9721. The Macedonian version bears N000-9722 to N000-9723.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, the document that is displayed in front of you, the Macedonian version, drawing your attention to the -- what appears to be the second full paragraph. Do you see your name mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And the top of this document is entitled "Official Note Number 1131." Do you see that at the top in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the date indicated on this document in the upper left corner is 12 August 2001; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this document has, at the very top, language indicating that it is from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And on the second page, which is N000-9721, the Macedonian version -- oh, I'm sorry, N000-9723 of the Macedonian version, N000-9721 of the English version. Could we go to the second page, please? Witness, do you see your name indicated on this page and your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention - if we could go back to the first page, please, of both versions. If I could draw your attention to the last part of the page before the Roman numeral II, that last paragraph before the Roman numeral II on the Macedonian version. Do you see that? Starting with: "According to."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this paragraph says: "According to statements of people from the security forces who handed over the above-mentioned persons, together with weapons and ammunition, to me these persons were active with fire-arms against the security forces in the zone of military activities from different houses and directions in Ljuboten village." Do you see that? Is that an accurate statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: This is absolutely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could tender that document, please, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to object, Your Honours. The witness was shown a document. We don't know whether the witness recognises the document -- this document. He -- it has not been shown to the witness in a proper manner. The witness was asked about a content of a document. The Prosecutor plans to call other witnesses and the authors of this document, and I think that that would be the right time to tender this document. Then -- only then we can talk about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you say that this is not an authentic document of the Ministry of Interior? Is that your proposition?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we do not speak about the authenticity of the document. We simply don't know what is the position of the Prosecution, because they -- do they claim that this is a fake document, that the content is fake? We do not know what is the position of the Prosecution. The witness did not recognise. Actually, he was not even asked to say whether he has ever -- has seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, he would probably not ever have seen this document before, because it's not a document that is his or would be shown to him, is it? The point, as I would understand it, of the Prosecution in seeking to tender an apparently authentic ministry document is that it gives some confirmation of some parts of the account being given by this witness; namely, that on that date, he, with a number of other people whom seem to be the people he has identified, were taken into custody and driven to Skopje, and, as I understand it, on that basis that this is put forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in line with the decision you made regarding the documents, I understood that the best manner, the most proper manner to document -- to show a document to the witness is that the document that he can recognise. As far as we can understand, according to the witnesses proposed for the next week, we have the author of this document and we think that would be the right moment and the proper manner to have this document shown because -- and to be tendered in -- in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. MS. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. As the Chamber has heard, the witness can establish the relevance and probative value of this document. He is mentioned in this document. It refers to statements or at least infers that statements were gathered -- or information was gathered from him or regarding him. So he certainly could speak to whether or not the contents of this document are true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How do you say it becomes admissible?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's my understanding that the -- both Defence counsel have not disputed the authenticity of the document and, again, the document is relevant with respect to this witness because he -- he is mentioned in this document. It contribute -- it refers to conduct or activities that this witness supposedly participated in, and this witness is denying that that occurred. So its relevant and probative value is clear, with this witness's testimony that this statement attributed to his conduct and activities is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received, Ms. Residovic. There being no dispute as to its authenticity, the document is clearly dealing with facts which are directly the subject of this witness's evidence and is -- he is named in it, in a context consistent with his evidence. In that respect, it offers some support of his evidence. It also contradicts his evidence in other material represents as he acknowledges, and which version of that might prove to be true will depend on the evidence of other witnesses. So this document is not being admitted that on the basis of what is written there is true. It doesn't establish that one way or the other, but it is it an official record about what happened to this document -- this witness, so that is one of the matters that will be taken into account as the Chamber comes to consider what actually did happen on that day. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P23, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Under seal?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could show the witness the next document in line at tab 14 of the witness binders provided today. It's 65 ter 148, bearing ERN, Macedonian version N000-7278. The English version is the same N000-7278-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, drawing your attention to what looks to be the second full paragraph of this document that begins with a person's name; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in that paragraph, do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in the top of this document it says it is the Official Note number 535. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It also refers as a subject to an official conversation carried out in the subject line here, right below the number 535. It indicates that subject is an official conversation carried out with the persons taken over from the village of Ljuboten? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the date on the top in the corner -- left corner of the document is 13 August 2001; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at the very top of the document, it indicates that is the MOI of the Republic of Macedonia; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, there appears to be the a typo in the English version of the document that I see here. The date is indicated as 12 August 2001, and I believe looking at the Macedonian version which is the original version is should read 13/8/2001, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Drawing your attention, Witness, to the second -- what looks to be actually the third full paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Motoike, when you say the original is 13, do you mean that when you look at the original it shows at the top of the document the date 13 August, but in the first paragraph of the body of the document it shows the date 12 August?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Sorry, thank you. For clarification, I'm referring to the very top left corner that indicates on the Macedonian version 13/8/2001. However, in the English version in the top left-hand corner of the English version, it indicates a date of 12 August 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, in my English version, it shows 13, if that's any help.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Perhaps we're operating on better hard copies than the e-court copies. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, drawing your attention to the third full paragraph of this document, and if I could just highlight a particular sentence in this document and read it to you. It says that: "The aforementioned stated that they noticed several terrorists who fought with their gun -- with guns in their hands, but allegedly they themselves -- they have not participated in the clashes but they wanted to escape from the village or some of them wanted to surrender to the security forces because they had not taken part in the fights." Is that a true statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: It is not correct, because here it says that we were trying to escape, and we were in the basement. They came and took us from the basement. This is a big lie. They want to represent us as a threat, as someone who can do them something bad. And that is not what happened. We were in the basement, and they came and took us from the basement. Here it says that we were fighting. If there was fighting between us and them, then there would have been wounded people. Were there any wounded people? Of course there were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, could I stop you there, please. So there is a reference here to terrorists who had been fighting with weapons on their hands. Is that statement true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No, not at all. This is what I'm saying. It's not true at all. They should prove it, if they found some arms on us. I didn't have any weapon. If I did have a weapon, I would have certainly shot and used the weapon and wounded maybe some policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if I could just draw your attention to the -- what appears to the fourth paragraph of this same document. It says that: "In connection to the weapons and ammunition that was found with them during their arrest, they stated that they had not used them. The following weapons and ammunition was found at the place where these persons were found and arrested." And it lists an AP automatic rifle, an AP Chinese production with a particular number. Is that particular statement true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Not at all. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if I could ask you: Do you recall making any statements -- any of the statements -- well, let me ask you this first. It indicates at the very top -- if we could go to the very top left corner of the document. It indicates that it's submitted by a person who is named Toskovski Blagoja; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall having any conversation with this particular person at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I cannot say that I met someone. Even though, as I told you, when we were in hospital, they asked -- forced us to sign, and I did sign, but as to what document I signed, they know better. They forced me to accept to sign, and I did put my signature. They know very well in what condition. I was under duress, you know, and I don't know what I have signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, before we get into that topic, could we --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could I ask the Chamber, please, to tender that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence understood well your previous decision, and we will act in accordance with that decision, but bearing in mind that a similar document was shown as the previous one, for the record we want to give the identical objections, aware that you will be -- that you will decide in the identical manner. We are doing this, Your Honours, because we do not know at all what is the position of the Prosecution about the content of this document. They will call the author of the document. We would like to know whether the Prosecution thinks that this document is a false one, so we could prepare for the cross-examination of their own witness. That is the reason why we are repeating the objections that we had before. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, and your position is fully understood. But could I suggest that you can assume that the Prosecution, like the witness, is taking the position that much of the contents of this document and the previous one do not accurately record what actually occurred. And you can, I think, safely proceed on that basis in dealing with your cross-examination. That would be my reading of the position, Ms. Motoike, if I'm misled Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour. And, additionally, if we could ask that -- if the Chamber is going to admit it, that it be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since we understood that there are two English translations, we would be asked to be told which translation would be accepted; the translation that you have, or the translation in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will be dealing with the translation in English which accords with the original; that is, the one that shows the date 13 August 2001 in the heading at the top left of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just to assist Defence, my case manager has indicated that we are in the process of uploading into e-court the version that the Chamber has in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now the document will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P24, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move on and show the witness 65 ter 225, which is tab 16 of the binders provided today. This document bears Macedonian version ERN N000-1248 through N000-1250.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, there's a document presently before you. If I can draw your attention to the second paragraph, which falls right underneath the word "decision." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Does that second paragraph of the first page, does that second paragraph have -- indicate your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in this document at the top there, I have already mentioned it, but for the record, does that middle word under the first paragraph say "decision"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: It doesn't say "decision."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It does say "decision"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I don't see the word "decision." It -- it says what is given by the -- what is written by the hospital, like a medical record.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm asking -- I'm sorry, I think you're referring to the first paragraph. The word right underneath the first paragraph, what is that word?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may assist, I think that the witness is looking at the previous document. He should be told to look at the document that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, I believe the document is displayed before you on the screens. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in -- underneath the first full paragraph -- well, I think we need to ask this again. I apologise. The second --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes, now I see it. It says "decision."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And does it say your name there in the second full paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could change -- switch to the second page of the document in both versions, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you see at the bottom a signature -- the bottom of the second page there, does it say "public prosecutor"?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I see Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're waiting for the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting, but comparing the translation in the Macedonian version, I think the translation is not very well. I think it is -- this is not a decision Macedonian but a resolution. The very word says "reshenie," so reshenie, a resolution, and a decision are not the same thing, because the courts make various decisions and one of the types of decisions is the resolution. That's what I wanted to warn about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Apostolski. I'm sure we will learn more about some of these things as the case progresses, but at the moment we have what is an official translation with the word "decision." If you think it is material to your case, you might take it up with the translation service to see whether some correction should be made to the official translation. I'm not sure that any particular significance attaches to the difference between resolution and decision at this point, but that will be a matter for you to judge. Thank you. Yes, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, drawing your attention to the signature line that is right above the word "note," towards the bottom of the second page of this document. Do you see that it says "juvenile court judge"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the date right above that juvenile court judge indication, is that date 14 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could change to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Witness, in that paragraph that is directly under the word "decision," actually the second paragraph under the word "decision," do you see that it says: "Is to be remanded in custody for 30 days from 11.30 hours on 14 August 2001 to 11.30 hours on 13 September 2001 because there are legal grounds to remand him in custody pursuant to Article 184, paragraph 1." And then it goes on to say other items. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall -- if you can, do you recall that you were remanned in custody for 30 days at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Can you please be more explicit about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Certainly. Sorry, I used "remanded." Were you in custody during that time-period which is indicated at 14 August 2001 until 13th September 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I was in custody.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this document please be tendered under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P25, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could show another document next in line in the witness binder, tab 17, 65 ter 12.2, bearing ERN N000-4410, N000-4418, which is the Macedonian version, and the English translation bears the same number with ET at the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this document? And if I can draw your attention -- if I can draw your attention to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Usher, could we go to page 3 of the document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you have a hard copy in front of you. Can you tell me on page 3, if I can draw your attention to page 3, can you tell me in the first full paragraph, under Roman number II, if that is your name indicated in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 1 of the document, please, in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Witness, do you see the first page at the top left corner, it says "Public Prosecutor's Office"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you see that in the middle, towards of top of this document, on the first page, it says: "To the lower court Skopje II, Skopje." On the first page of the document right underneath the date, which is indicated. Do you see that it says: "To the lower court, Skopje II"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you see the date in the left-hand corner, upper corner? It says 26th September, 2001.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you see underneath Roman numeral I, do you see that it says "indictment" there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And have you seen this document previously, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention to page 3 of your hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Usher, if we could go to page 3 on both versions on the screens as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to the second full paragraph, it says: "Between 0800 and 1.200 on 12 August 2001, in the village of Ljuboten, Skopje, they participated in armed conflict as combatants against the Republic of Macedonia in a way that during intensive military actions, they acted against the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia stationed in the vicinity of the village with infantry fire-arms and ammunition up to the moment when they were forced to retreat, at which point they abandoned their fighting positions and threw away their weapons and equipment, with the aim of avoiding responsibility. But at that moment, they were intercepted by the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia who had begun to clear the area, during which time military actions intensified, and they were arrested and part of the weapons and equipment were seized from them." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that a -- is that a true statement in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Far from it. Far from it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this be tendered under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P26, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we can go to the exhibit next in line in the witness binder at tab 18, 65 ter 12.5, bearing ERN in the Macedonian version N000-4423, N000-4425. And the English version bears the same ERN with ET at the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to draw your attention to the second full paragraph of the first page of this document before you. Do you see that your name -- is your name mentioned in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could go to the word right above the paragraph that you've indicated your name is in, does that word say "ruling"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could go to -- Mr. Usher, with your assistance - page 3, which is the last page of each of the versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, in the hard copy, are you looking at the last page of the document? And drawing your attention to the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. I can't see it very well here. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And just above -- in this paragraph that's indicated on this page, does it indicate that it is from the deputy head of the court, the council?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Actually, I'm sorry, Mr. Usher. Could we go to the page before -- in the Macedonian version, could we go to the page that would be N000-4425, which I believe is page 2 of the Macedonian version. I apologise. Could we scroll to the bottom, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, looking at the second page of the Macedonian version, do you see the very bottom of that page? Does it indicate that there's a stamp with a deputy head of the court, the council? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, have you seen this document previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: In the prison, when they extended the detention that we received such papers. But I can tell you that they did what they wanted with these documents because we were in their hands. For me, this is not a proper document, even though it has a seal, because they have written in it whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to the first page of the document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Witness, I will direct your attention to the first page in it's hard copy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In the paragraph under ruling, the first sentence, it reads: "The motion of the investigating judge of the lower court Skopje II, Skopje KI number 436/01 of 11 September 2001 for the continuation of custody for the accused." And it names, among others, you there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, my name is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And it indicates in that same paragraph that that motion is granted, at the very last words; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this be tendered under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P27, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Going to the document that is next in line in the witness binder, tab 22, which is 65 ter 10.15, bears ERN 0463-8814. The English version is ET 0463-8814, 0463-8814.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you have the hard copy of the this document in front of you. In the Macedonian version, do you see at number 7 on the first -- on the only page of this document, do you see number 7? Is that your name indicated there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in the middle, in bold of this document, does it say particular report and then following that, does it say: "... related to our criminal charges submitted under the herein above mentioned number and against the following persons"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At the very top of the document, if we could scroll up there, please. In the left-hand corner at the top, does it say: "Ministry of Interior, OVR-OOR, Cair"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is the date, right underneath that, "27 August 2001"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you see right underneath "Skopje" towards the right of the document on that page, it says to basic --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It says to basic public prosecutor, Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I can direct your attention to the paragraph that follows the numbers, that number 10 on the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could scroll down, Mr. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And that paragraph states: "Attached to this report are an expert testimony (analysis) of fire-arm 10.26-30027/1 dated 16/08/2001 prepared by MOI of RM Sector for Criminal Techniques and a photo album which are in relation to the fire-arm seized of the above mentioned persons from the village of Ljuboten who were apprehended under charges they committed criminal act of terrorism." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that statement true, with respect to the mention of the fire-arms seized?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Not at all. Not at all. It's not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is with respect to the charges that they committed the criminal act of terrorism; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No, not at all. I told you even earlier that if we were terrorists, then they wouldn't be able to imprison me but we were unarmed and so they did what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If that document may be tendered, Your Honours, under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P28, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Ms. Motoike, we must have the second break at this point, and we will resume at 6.00.

utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, earlier in your testimony, you referred to signing a document at the hospital. It was page 46 of the transcript, lines 9 through 14. Do you see -- if we could go to page 2 of the Macedonian and English versions, please. In the hard copy that is before you, do you see a signature at the very bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you also see a signature on page 3 of the same document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And on page 4 of the document, at the very bottom after the typing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of the signatures on this page -- these pages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: The third page, as I said earlier, they forced me to sign this document. On the third page, it is my signature; while on the fourth and the second, it's not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we can look at page 1, please, of both documents. Actually, the Macedonian version, if we could go -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you the hard copy. You are looking at page 1. Can I direct your attention to the name that appears right after the date on that document. Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is the date of this document -- is the date indicated as 15 August 2001 on this first page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The date is the one you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2, please, on both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in the first -- actually, the first paragraph after the indented paragraph, that first sentence that begins with the interrogation. It states that: "The interrogation of the" - and I won't say that person - "started at 1340-hours in the premises of the General City Hospital Skopje where the person was admitted." Does that say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall having a conversation at the General City Hospital --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I only signed a document. I did not speak to anyone at any time. I only signed a document under duress. It was not out of my free will.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we go to the last page of the document again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, drawing your attention to very bottom of this last page on the right bottom corner, it says "the juvenile judge." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in the left there, it says "court clerk," and then next to that, it says "Defence attorney." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then drawing your attention to -- if we could go to page 4, which I believe is in both versions. Witness, you have in front of you a hard copy of the Macedonian version, the page 4 of the English translation, I believe, is up on the screen. Could you look at the hard copy, please, and drawing your attention to this first paragraph. Do you see the first paragraph on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, for a brief moment, may we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether or not this document that is before you is the same document that you say you were forced to sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: As I already said earlier, I do not know what document I signed because I was not conscious. I cannot lie here and say, Yes, this is the document --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we tender that, please, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.
