utterances.text: Moving on next in line, tab 24 of the witness binder, 65 ter 10.28. If we could please show the witness that document bearing ERN N -- bearing ERN Macedonian version 0463-8827, and the English translation is ET N046-38827, but that might be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to the bottom left corner of this document, do you see a signature there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No, it's not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that your name that's signed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, the name is mine, but the signature is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is this document -- if we could go up to the upper left corner. Does this document say, Minister of the Interior OVR-OOR Cair, on the top left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this document dated 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: As I said earlier, maybe this was not the correct date. Maybe the document was created at a later date, referred -- referring to that date. As I said, I was in a proper condition only a month later.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, I'm only asking you whether or not you see that this document in the upper left-hand corner is dated 12 August, 2001; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you also see that in the middle here of the document in bold, it says: "Certificate on temporary seized possessions." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph following that bolded -- those bolded word, it says -- at the very ending of that sentence, it says: "Seize the following possessions in temporary custody." And then it names at (1): "10 bullets for AP (automatic rifle, caliber 7,62). Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is that paragraph, including that number, that point at that number 1, is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No, far from the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this be tendered, please, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P30, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could show the witness next in line tab 25, it's a document which is 65 ter 10.12, bearing Macedonian version ERN 0463-8808, 0463-8810; English version is the same numbers with ET in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you have the hard copy Macedonian version in front of you. If I can just draw your attention to page 2, number 7. Is that your name indicated there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 1. And, Witness, looking at the hard copy, page 1. In the upper left-hand corner, do you see the words "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is the date right below that, 13 August, 2001, is that indicated on the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And does it say, "To: Basic public prosecutor Skopje," in the bolded words below the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And does it also say in bolded words in the centre of the document, "criminal charges"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could go to the very last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, on the last page, at the very bottom, do you see that it says, "head officer of OVR Cair"?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have suggested to us a while ago to address the CLSS regarding the translations. I would just like to say that we have noted several of the same documents that are translated differently, a decision as a ruling and the ruling as a decision. We can see a document whereby they said that that is the criminal charges, that is a completely different document. In importance of the criminal procedure, this should be a criminal report. Just for the transcript, I would like to draw the attention to those facts, and we will address the CLSS. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, I had asked you a question as to whether or not at the bottom of this document, in the left, do you see it says "head officer of OVR Cair"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the top paragraph -- I'm sorry, we have both English versions published right now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: It's okay. I have the Macedonian before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On the last page, there is a paragraph that starts with: "The afore-identified persons." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And that paragraph says: "The afore-identified persons continued with these operations until 12.00 a.m. when they deserted their combat positions, and they left their fire-arm and equipment. Actually, they threw away part of the equipment. All these they did it in order to avoid liability for the terrorist activities they had committed." Is that an accurate statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No, not at all. How can they write something like this? They should be ashamed. I was a 13-year-old.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we tender this exhibit, please, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P31 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Motoike. Now, is it -- Ms. Residovic, do you wish to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much. I would ask just whether we are in an open or a private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're in open.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. M-017. I am Edina Residovic and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, I'm defending Mr. Ljube Boskoski. I will ask you, Mr. M-017, for a better understanding of the question that I am about to ask and for the answer -- your answer to that question to wait for a while for my question to be interpreted and only then to give your answer, so the interpreters would have the time to interpret both the question and the answer and so Their Honours and the colleagues in the courtroom could understand. Did you understand me, Mr. M-017?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like to ask that we move into a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, just for the sake of clarification, could we spend a few more minutes in a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your family was one of farmers, is that correct, of cattle breeders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No one was employed in a public institution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You lived modestly. One could even say that life was quite difficult. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before 2001, you were never summoned to a court or a police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Who would summon me?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether it is correct that you have never been summoned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: We never had a problem before 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-017, that after the events you have given statements many times to the press and the international organisations? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I haven't given any statements to the journalists, but I may have given a statement to some foreign organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is shown ID 33, page 1D 0402 and 1D 0404. So have I stated correctly, 1D 33, page 1D 0402, 1D 0404.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have stated that you may have given statements to some foreigners, to some international organisations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 5th of January, 2002, you have given a statement to the OSCE; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: You just read out to me what you want, and then I will say if it's correct. I told you earlier maybe I have, but first you have to read out to me what the contents of my supposed statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You say here that on the 5th of January, 2002, you have had an interview with Elvara Balastrone [phoen]. He's had an interview with you. I could not read it now because we are in a public session now. But do you remember that you have given an international organisation a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I don't remember, but as I said, I would kindly ask you to read it to me, and then I can say whether it's true or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to the International Committee of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. 017, you have given many statements to the investigator of the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have given statements many times to the investigators of the Prosecutor of the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The first statement was given by you on the 30th of March, 2003; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is shown a document without it being shown to the public, 65 ter number 1D 26, page 1D 0315; Macedonian number page 1D 0321.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you recognise your signature in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I don't see my signature here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the English text?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please show the witness the page ID 316.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes. Now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please show the witness page 1D 0320; Macedonian version 0325?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see here in the English text and recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Below the first paragraph, on the top of the English text, your name is written; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it you who wrote this name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were interviewed by the ICTY investigator, you would sign every page then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You do not speak the English language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But whenever you would be giving a statement, you had an interpreter for the Albanian language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After having the statement translated to you, you have stated that everything you said in that statement was correct and that corresponds to the best of your recollection about that event; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have given the next statement to the Prosecutor on the 12th of August, 2003; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: I think so. You may read the statement back to me, and then I can tell you. You're just asking me whether I signed, but I would like to know what is it in this statement, so that I know that it's me who has given it and not just ask me whether I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you immediately the document 1D 27, page 1D 0328; Macedonian 1D 0339.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I ask that this document is also not shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you then recognise your signature on this page of the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this statement of the 12th of August was also signed on every page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask now that the witness is shown the document 1D 28, page 0349; and Macedonian 1D 0354.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document which states that you have given an interview also on the 25th of October, 2003, to the investigator of the Prosecutor of the ICTY. Is it correct that on that date, you have also given a statement to the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is your signature found on this document as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask now that the witness is shown the document number 1D 29, page 1D 0359. And I ask that this document is also not available to the public. Have you signed this document, sir? I apologise, I did not indicate the number of the Macedonian page, but it is already displayed on the screen. Tell me, have you, on the 23rd of April this year, so it means 2007, also given certain additions and corrections to your previous statements to the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature on this document as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that after the arrival to The Hague on the 6th of May, 2007, in the preparations for your today's testimony by the Prosecutor, that the Prosecutor has shown you certain documents and that also after that, you made certain comments? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question, because I'm not clear?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived to The Hague, is it correct that the Prosecutor has shown you certain documents, and that you then also signed a document with comments that you made when the Prosecutor was showing you those documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask that the witness is shown the document 1D 41, and page 1D 0507 and 1D 0509.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I would ask the witness to just tell me whether that is the document that I have mentioned and have you signed this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have just finished authenticating the prior statements of this witness. Before I start the examination regarding certain questions, maybe it would be time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that is a convenient time, Ms. Residovic. We will resume tomorrow morning -- oh, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very sorry for the interruption. I'd like to bring something to the attention of the Trial Chamber that the Prosecution has already discussed with Defence counsel. Obviously, the cross -- excuse me, the direct examination of this witness took a bit longer than the Prosecution expected. Defence counsel have told me that they believe they will need until -- they will need the full day tomorrow to complete their cross-examination of this witness. Therefore, with your leave, I will not bring the following witness who was scheduled. I believe that was M-012. We will, with your leave, put that witness over until next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber would indicate that there will be no witness called tomorrow at the end of the evidence of this witness, and we would encourage both Defence counsel to look carefully at their cross-examination and their coordination to ensure that cross-examination finishes tomorrow. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
